To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have improved the retrieval of CH4 and CO  from SCIAMACHY measurements in the solar occultation mode and that the first stratosphere CO2 profiles from SCIAMACH Y are available.
we have derived the first SCIAMACHY CH4 stratospheric profiles from solar occultation data.
we have developed an improved retrieval method for the SCIAMACHY CH4 and CO  2 solar occultation measurements and have derived stratospheric CH4 and CO 2 profiles from the SCIAMACH Y data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the retrieval of atmospheric parameters from SCIAMACH Y solar occultation spectra.
the derivation of high-quality stratospheric profiles from SCIAMACH Y solar occultation measurements and their use to estimate CH4 and CO  2 trends.
the derivation of high-quality stratospheric profiles for CH4 and CO  from solar occultation measurements with the SCIAMACHY instrument.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SCIAMACHY ONPD data set is a valuable and useful data set for the stratosphere, which can contribute to the understanding of the stratospheric chemistry and the stratosphere–troposphere exchange.
the SCIAMACHY CH4 and CO profiles have a good potential for stratospheric studies, however, the current accuracy of the profiles is still too poor to be used for trend studies.

The main takeaway from our work is that

we have developed a retrieval approach which can be applied for the derivation of stratospheric profiles from SCIAMACHy solar occultation measurements and which is also suitable for the retrieval of other gases.
